atomicity.reason: One shall-clause computing one quantity (the sustained-load share) as a two-level function of one condition (10 s average below vs at or above 250 A); the "and" joins the complementary arms of that single function, not independent obligations, in the same style as the sibling swreqs.

comprehensibility.reason: Intelligible on its own: it defines the sustained-load share in the same sentence, gives both branches with their numbers and explains 320 A inline as the current drawn at full permitted power; "power limit component", "permitted discharge power" and "full permitted power" are used as in the sibling swreqs and in REQ_POWER_DERATING and REQ_THERMAL_ACTUATOR_FAILSAFE.

feasibility.reason: Implementable (a windowed mean plus a two-level share) and consistent with REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT (the 250 A cap is below the 320 A full-power draw, which is below the 350 A trip) and with the 250 A continuous rating, but it holds the current at 250 A only through a fixed power-to-current anchor (320 A at full power) that appears nowhere upstream: current for a given power varies with pack voltage (I = P/V), so at a lower pack voltage the 78.125 % share draws more than 250 A and the 30 A (about 9 %) margin to the 350 A trip shrinks.
feasibility.suggestion: Record the 320 A as a sourced assumption or parameter (the pack voltage or operating point it holds at, linked to its source), and either derive the cap from the measured pack voltage or close the loop on the measured current, or add an explicit margin so the requirement to never exceed 250 A holds over the pack voltage range.

parent_fit.reason: Defines exactly the sustained-load limit that ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR says it computes from the pack discharge current, with the figures of REQ_SUSTAINED_DISCHARGE_LIMIT (250 A, trailing 10 s average, engaged when the average "reaches" 250 A = at or above, released when it "falls below"); it covers the distinct sustained-load part and leaves the ramp and the minimum to SWREQ_TEMP_DERATE_RAMP and SWREQ_LIMIT_MINIMUM.

unambiguity.reason: Core meaning is clear, but "the pack discharge current averaged over the trailing 10 s" has underspecified edge cases that change the outcome: charge-direction (regeneration) current as 0 A or as negative (8 s at 330 A plus 2 s at -100 A averages 264 A one way and 244 A the other, i.e. 78.125 % vs 100 %), the average with less than 10 s of samples at start-up, and a missing or invalid current.
unambiguity.suggestion: Say whether charge-direction samples count as 0 A or as negative, what the average and the share are until 10 s of valid samples exist, and which share applies while the current is invalid or unavailable.

verifiability.reason: Every threshold is explicit (250 A, 10 s, 320 A, 100 %, "below" vs "at or above"), so constant-current tests decide cleanly, but boundary tests have no unique oracle: no evaluation cadence or response time for the share to follow the average, no definition of the window edge (N vs N+1 samples, sample- vs time-weighted mean), and no tolerance or rounding direction for 78.125 % (rounding up would exceed the 250 A cap).
verifiability.suggestion: State the averaging as a sliding arithmetic mean over a named sample period, state that the share is re-evaluated every named cycle (e.g. 100 ms) and follows the average within one cycle, and give the capped share as 78.125 % with a tolerance or "rounded down".

summary: A crisp, well-traced piecewise limit (100 % below, 250 A / 320 A = 78.125 % at or above a 10 s average of 250 A) that matches ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR, REQ_SUSTAINED_DISCHARGE_LIMIT and REQ_PACK_OVERCURRENT, but it leaves the averaging edge cases, response time and tolerance open and rests on an unsourced, voltage-dependent 320 A anchor.
